spec.sequence: Coming down the track from Greenspring, a cairn and a totem mark where it meets the road. West along the road the planks of the inlet deck show low over the marsh.
spec.wayfinding: The road runs west from the track head, down to the inlet deck and on to the river crossing.

spec.sequence: Coming south-east along the road from Stormhold, a cairn marks the head of the river crossing and the planks run straight across the marsh to the stone steps.
spec.wayfinding: Across the planks, up the steps and along the top of the bank.

spec.value: The Border road was laid on a Dunmer line from Stormhold to Thorn. Below Greenspring it meets the river marsh and an inlet stream. Its keepers carry it over both on piled timber.
Nobody lives on the crossings. The village above keeps the planks because its trade goes out along this road.
The marsh rots the piles in a few seasons. The village above has to keep replacing them.
The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot and crosses water only where it must, at the inlet mouth and at one reach of the river marsh.
A causeway of stone would replace the planks if anyone paid for one.

value.loreSource: route record route.road.stormhold-thorn (worn; long timber bridges patched) and world/sources/routes/route-structure-exemplars.json
value.why: A stretch of road with two plank crossings, stone steps and road marks; nobody lives on it.

spec.orientationWhy: A cold fire ring on the flat above the inlet, with rocks along both bends and a cairn at the west head of the inlet deck.
